mcat_description.short: Toilet partitions are modular cubicle partition systems installed in commercial and public washrooms to create private stalls, sold as complete units comprising panels, doors, pilasters, and hardware.
mcat_description.long: Toilet partitions are prefabricated, modular washroom divider systems used to create individual privacy stalls in commercial, institutional, and public restrooms. In the Indian market, they are predominantly manufactured from High-Pressure Laminate (HPL) compact board — valued for its moisture resistance, anti-bacterial surface, and durability under heavy use — with stainless steel, nylon-hardware, HDPE, PVC, and WPC variants serving different budget and application tiers. Systems are sold as complete cubicle units (panels + door + pilasters + hardware) and are customised to project dimensions, number of compartments, and finish preferences. Key installation environments include shopping malls, corporate offices, airports, schools, hospitals, and public facilities across India.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, toilet partitions are commercially known as 'toilet cubicles' or 'bathroom partitions' — the terms are used interchangeably by buyers and sellers. HPL (High-Pressure Laminate) compact board is the dominant material, preferred for its moisture resistance, anti-bacterial surface, and durability in high-traffic commercial environments; this is confirmed across multiple Indian manufacturer sites (Restloo, T-Line, Megha Systems, Merino Restrooms, Galaxy Cubicle India). Hardware series — stainless steel (SS) vs nylon — is a key differentiator that buyers explicitly specify, as evidenced by call data showing 'SS Series' and 'Nylon Series' as distinct product lines. Secondary materials include HDPE solid plastic (premium, graffiti-resistant), PVC (budget segment), WPC, and powder-coated steel. Stylam and Greenlam are recognised Indian HPL board brands whose names appear in buyer search queries, indicating brand-aware procurement for the board material. Installation types include floor-mounted, ceiling-hung (top-hung), and free-floor (no floor rail) systems — the latter being preferred in premium commercial projects for hygiene and cleaning ease. Panel thickness typically ranges from 12mm to 25mm, with 12mm being standard for most commercial applications and 25mm for heavy-duty or premium installations. The market is project-driven: buyers are primarily interior contractors, architects, and facility managers procuring for commercial fit-outs, with malls, airports, offices, and schools being the dominant end-use segments. No BIS IS standard specific to toilet partitions was found in available sources (single source — low confidence); the product is governed by general construction material quality norms rather than a dedicated Indian standard.
